items.title: Interconnection queue growth and permitting signals increasing project timing risk
items.lede: Signals from queue filings and permitting backlogs indicate interconnection pipelines are growing faster than queue-processing capacity, increasing the risk of multi-year delays for some transmission and distribution projects.
items.body: Signals from queue filings and permitting backlogs indicate interconnection pipelines are growing faster than queue-processing capacity, increasing the risk of multi-year delays for some transmission and distribution projects.
items.summary: Signals from queue filings and permitting backlogs indicate interconnection pipelines are growing faster than queue-processing capacity, increasing the risk of multi-year delays for some transmission and distribution projects.
items.why_it_matters: Interconnection and permitting slowdowns interact with supply-chain and manufacturing constraints; delays can concentrate procurement, stretch EPC capacity, and alter market timing for new resources.
items.action_for_readers: Monitor additional evidence before making operational or investment decisions.

lenses.engineering: Designs should include alternative connection options and phased commissioning to manage queue uncertainty.
lenses.business: Developers and EPCs should model schedule risk into contracts and financing assumptions.
lenses.policy: Regulators may need to adjust review resources or standardize studies to reduce backlog risk.
lenses.climate: Delays in bringing new low-carbon capacity online can affect near-term emissions trajectories.
lenses.history: Previous interconnection surges have produced long tail timelines and pushed policy reforms toward queue reform.
